acceptance.assertion: The locale resolver has a tested, documented context-sensitive priority contract: an explicit locale URL or deep link determines the current navigation and is never automatically overridden; on a neutral entry surface a locally stored manual UI-language choice wins; in Automatic mode the first supported entry from navigator.languages is used; unsupported or unavailable preferences fall back to English; and a user-activated language switch updates the stored choice.

The language control exposes an accessible Automatic – device language option alongside English and German, supports keyboard and assistive technology, clearly indicates the effective language and does not require location permission.

Manual and Automatic choices persist locally without cookies, accounts or network transmission; unavailable, blocked or corrupt storage fails safely without breaking the page or causing redirect loops.

Locale switches preserve applicable query parameters and URL fragments, do not overwrite an explicit shared locale URL merely because a different preference is stored, and never loop between English and German surfaces.

Changing UI language does not silently alter the catalogue content-language filter, country selection, proximity origin, radius, map position or other discovery state; UI language, content language and regional relevance remain separate axes.

Browser language matching handles ordered, case-insensitive BCP 47 tags including region and script subtags, chooses only supported UI locales and has regression coverage for de-DE, en-GB, mixed preference lists and unsupported languages.

Canonical generators, source assets, German and English public pages and the immutable release tree contain the same locale-selection contract with content-version references regenerated deterministically.

The exact implementation head passes focused JavaScript and Python i18n tests, full repository validation, responsive browser smoke, diff-bound self-review and all required GitHub checks; the complete UTF-8 plaintext diff is delivered before merge, followed by exact-SHA Pages and production readback.

approval.note: The user explicitly requested implementation through Grabowski. Work must start only after T032 is terminal and its overlapping i18n, generated-page, assets, browser and publication surfaces are released.

goal: Make Commonworld choose its user-interface language predictably and privately: preserve an explicit local user choice, honor an explicitly selected locale surface, otherwise use the ordered browser/device language preferences and fall back to English, without deriving UI language from geolocation or coupling it to content-language and regional discovery filters.
